headline: Trust Is the New Currency
thesis: From faculty afraid to disclose AI use to districts that now buy on trust over features, today's stories show education deciding whom and what to believe.
summary: Tuesday's digest centers on trust. Inside Higher Ed reports that most faculty now use AI in some form, but with no shared line between AI-assisted writing and misconduct, fear is discouraging disclosure in what it calls an AI 'witch hunt.' A companion opinion piece asks what colleges' claims of 'AI leadership' really mean. On the K-12 side, an EdTech Digest column built on interviews with twelve district leaders finds they now weigh vendor trust above price or features, with some moving to outcomes-based contracts. Federal policy also moved: Inside Higher Ed lays out where the international student crackdown stands after court losses, with a proposed OPT fee as the next fight. A Philadelphia Fed study suggests new graduate loan caps are unlikely to reduce defaults, and NSF data show first-time science and health grad enrollment fell about 10%. On standards, 1EdTech's Learning Impact Award nominations have closed, with finalists to be notified by Nov. 30, and the QTI survey closes the same day.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · NOVEMBER 24, 2026 · Items were gathered through web search because direct page fetches were blocked in this run. Several sources published nothing new today and show their most recent items.
